facts.f: Mandarin Chinese has more native speakers than any other language.
facts.e: Native speakers are people who learned it as their first language.

facts.f: Hindi is written in the Devanagari script.
facts.e: Marathi, Nepali and Sanskrit are also written in Devanagari.

facts.f: Sanskrit is one of the oldest languages in the world.
facts.e: The Rigveda, one of the oldest known texts, is in an early form of Sanskrit.

facts.f: Tamil was the first language to be declared a Classical Language of India, in 2004.
facts.e: Tamil has a literature that is more than 2,000 years old.

facts.f: A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards.
facts.e: 'Madam', 'level' and 'racecar' are palindromes.

facts.f: 'Malayalam' is a palindrome.
facts.e: Spell it backwards: M-A-L-A-Y-A-L-A-M. It is the same!

facts.f: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog' uses every letter of the English alphabet.
facts.e: A sentence that uses every letter is called a pangram.

facts.f: The English alphabet has 26 letters. Five of them, a, e, i, o and u, are vowels.
facts.e: The letter y sometimes works like a vowel too, as in 'sky'.

facts.f: Many English words come from Indian languages.
facts.e: 'Shampoo', 'jungle', 'bungalow', 'pyjamas', 'cot' and 'loot' all came into English from India.

facts.f: 'Yoga', 'guru', 'karma' and 'avatar' are English words that come from Sanskrit.
facts.e: Words borrowed from another language are called loanwords.

facts.f: Synonyms are words with the same or similar meanings. Antonyms have opposite meanings.
facts.e: 'Big' and 'large' are synonyms. 'Hot' and 'cold' are antonyms.

facts.f: Homophones sound the same but have different meanings and spellings.
facts.e: 'Sea' and 'see', and 'flower' and 'flour' are homophones.

facts.f: Onomatopoeia means words that sound like what they describe.
facts.e: 'Buzz', 'sizzle', 'splash' and 'tick-tock' are examples.

facts.f: Braille is a system of raised dots that lets blind people read by touch.
facts.e: It was invented by Louis Braille, who was blind himself, and first published in 1829.

facts.f: India has its own sign language, Indian Sign Language.
facts.e: Deaf people use hand shapes, movements and facial expressions to communicate.

facts.f: 'E' is the most common letter in English writing.
facts.e: That is why it is worth only one point in many word games.

facts.f: The word 'laser' started as an acronym.
facts.e: It stands for Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation.

facts.f: The idiom 'a piece of cake' means something very easy.
facts.e: Idioms are phrases whose meaning is different from the meaning of each word.

facts.f: To 'break the ice' means to start a friendly conversation when people feel shy.
facts.e: It has nothing to do with real ice!

facts.f: The word 'alphabet' comes from the first two Greek letters, alpha and beta.
facts.e: In the same way, Hindi's 'varnamala' means a garland of letters.

facts.f: Urdu, Arabic and Persian are written from right to left.
facts.e: Hindi, English and Tamil are written from left to right.

facts.f: Japanese uses three scripts: hiragana, katakana and kanji.
facts.e: Kanji characters came from Chinese writing.

facts.f: Most of Emperor Ashoka's edicts were written in the Brahmi script.
facts.e: Many later Indian scripts, including Devanagari and Tamil, developed from Brahmi.

facts.f: Samuel Johnson published one of the most famous early English dictionaries in 1755.
facts.e: He worked on it for about nine years.

facts.f: A prefix is added to the start of a word, and a suffix to the end.
facts.e: 'Un-' in 'unhappy' is a prefix. '-less' in 'careless' is a suffix.

facts.f: 'Bi-' means two and 'tri-' means three.
facts.e: A bicycle has two wheels and a tricycle has three.

facts.f: 'Pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis' has 45 letters.
facts.e: It is a lung disease caused by breathing very fine ash and dust, and is one of the longest words in major English dictionaries.

facts.f: A group of fish is called a school, a group of bees a swarm, and a group of sheep a flock.
facts.e: Words for groups are called collective nouns.

facts.f: Esperanto is a language that was invented on purpose, in 1887.
facts.e: Its creator, L. L. Zamenhof, hoped it would help people of different countries talk to each other.

facts.f: Some English words have silent letters.
facts.e: The 'k' in 'knife', the 'w' in 'write' and the 'b' in 'thumb' are silent.

facts.f: Proper nouns, like names of people and places, start with a capital letter.
facts.e: Delhi, Ganga and Priya are proper nouns.

facts.f: Rhyming words end with the same sound.
facts.e: Cat, hat and bat all rhyme.

facts.f: Bengali is the second most spoken language in India.
facts.e: This is according to the 2011 Census. Hindi is the most spoken.

facts.f: 'Kindergarten' is a German word that means 'children's garden'.
facts.e: It was named by Friedrich Fröbel, who started the first kindergarten in 1837.

facts.f: 'Typewriter' can be typed using only the top row of letters on a keyboard.
facts.e: Try it: all its letters are in Q W E R T Y U I O P.

facts.f: An anagram is a word made by rearranging the letters of another word.
facts.e: 'Listen' and 'silent' are anagrams.

facts.f: Panini wrote the Ashtadhyayi, a famous grammar of Sanskrit, about 2,500 years ago.
facts.e: It has nearly 4,000 short rules.

facts.f: Hindi and Urdu share most of their everyday grammar and many words.
facts.e: Spoken together, they are sometimes called Hindustani.

facts.f: The dot over a small 'i' or 'j' is called a tittle.
facts.e: Most people never know it has a name!

facts.f: 'Bookkeeper' has three double letters in a row: oo, kk, ee.
facts.e: Try finding other words with double letters.

facts.f: 'Facetious' has all five vowels in alphabetical order: a, e, i, o, u.
facts.e: 'Abstemious' does too.

facts.f: The # symbol is called an octothorpe, a hash or a number sign.
facts.e: On social media, it is called a hashtag.

facts.f: 'Namaste' comes from Sanskrit and means 'I bow to you'.
facts.e: It is a respectful greeting used across India.
